info.description: The reviewed public HTTP and WebSocket contract for one Proctor installation. Operations are grouped by stable product areas, declare authentication and idempotency requirements explicitly, and return RFC 9457 Problem Details for documented failures.
info.title: Proctor Server API

post.description: Executes one to 200 independent existing-User administration rows. Each row retains the ordinary named aggregate, authorization, audit, mail, and idempotency semantics.
post.summary: Run one bounded typed existing-User academic administration batch

get.description: Lists Academic Periods visible through the caller's current Institution or Academic Unit authority, with stable owner-aware filtering. Periods describe effective academic time windows and do not themselves grant access to Classes or students.

parameters.description: Literal case-insensitive substring matched against name and display name.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Maximum number of visible Academic Periods to return.
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: List or search Academic Periods visible through authorized owner scopes

post.description: Creates one named Academic Period under the exact Institution or Academic Unit owner after terminal scope authorization. The inclusive start and exclusive end are Unix-millisecond instants, and an optional Idempotency-Key makes uncertain retries safe.
post.summary: Create an Institution- or Academic-Unit-owned Academic Period

delete.description: Archives one Academic Period only after proving that no active Class or enrollment still depends on it. History is retained, and the operation never cascades into Class deletion, membership termination, or student progression.
delete.summary: Archive an Academic Period with no active Classes or enrollments

get.description: Returns one Academic Period only when its durable owner is visible to the current principal. The response reports its owner and time bounds without implying access to every Class that references it.
get.summary: Get an Academic Period

patch.description: Applies a partial presentation or time-window update while preserving the Period's original owner. The authoritative transition rejects bounds that would invalidate dependent academic structure or conflict with current durable state.
patch.summary: Update an Academic Period without changing its owner

delete.description: Ends one exact effective Academic Unit membership after authorizing its current Unit scope. Historical dates and audit provenance remain durable, and ending membership does not silently remove affiliations, Roles, or scoped Role Bindings.
delete.summary: End organizational membership while retaining history

get.description: Lists the Academic Units visible to the current principal, optionally filtered by a literal case-insensitive name substring. Visibility is evaluated from current scoped authority and does not grant mutation permission. This bounded collection returns at most the requested limit.

parameters.description: Literal case-insensitive substring matched against name and display name.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Maximum number of Academic Units to return, from 1 through 200.
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: List or search Academic Units

post.description: Creates a top-level Academic Unit in the installation Institution after authoritative authorization. Supplying an optional Idempotency-Key makes an exact retry return the committed outcome; reusing the key with different input is a conflict. Server-owned identity and scope fields in the compatibility body are ignored.
post.summary: Create a root Academic Unit

curl --fail-with-body \
  --request POST \
  --url 'https://proctor.example.edu/api/v1/academic-units' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <access-token>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Idempotency-Key: docs-academic-unit-001' \
  --data '{"name":"computer-science","display_name":"Computer Science","description":"Teaching and research in computing."}'

delete.description: Archives one empty eligible Academic Unit while retaining hierarchy and audit history. Active descendants, Programmes, memberships, or authorization dependencies block the transition rather than being cascaded.

get.description: Returns one active Academic Unit only when it is visible through the principal's current scoped authority. The bounded projection identifies its Institution and parent but does not recursively include descendants or permission grants.
get.summary: Get an Academic Unit

patch.description: Applies a partial presentation update and can move the Unit beneath another valid parent after authorizing both sides. The transition rejects cycles, cross-Institution ownership, stale dependencies, and invalid hierarchy changes atomically.
patch.summary: Update or reparent an Academic Unit

get.description: Lists only the immediate active child Units beneath one authorized Academic Unit. The operation does not recursively flatten the hierarchy or broaden the caller's visibility to concealed descendants.
get.summary: List an Academic Unit's direct children

post.description: Creates one active Unit directly beneath the Academic Unit named by the route. Route scope is authoritative, and current permission is checked against the parent before the hierarchical relationship commits.
post.summary: Create a child Academic Unit

get.description: Searches Classes whose Programme hierarchy is owned by the authorized Academic Unit, using bounded stable traversal. Results expose Class structure only and never enroll students or grant Class-scoped permission.

parameters.description: Literal case-insensitive substring matched against name and display name.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Maximum number of Classes to return.
parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Search Classes owned by an Academic Unit

Proctor repeats deployment-capability and last-administrator-path checks in the authoritative transaction, can revoke Sessions affected by newly disabled methods, and requires both a strong recent interactive Session and an Idempotency-Key.

post.description: Consumes no Invitation yet; it exchanges the one-time claim for a short-lived, same-origin browser handle bound to that exact Invitation purpose. The response omits the original claim and prevents it from entering subsequent browser URLs or logs.
post.summary: Exchange an Invitation claim for a purpose-bound browser acceptance transaction

post.description: Creates the invited account and applies the immutable Invitation package through one purpose-bound browser handle. Password and profile inputs are validated, the handle is consumed atomically, and claim or credential material is never returned.
post.summary: Accept an account-creating Invitation through its browser transaction

post.description: Applies an eligible scoped Role Invitation to the exact already-authenticated User bound to the browser handle. It never relinks the package to another User and consumes the transaction atomically.
post.summary: Accept a scoped-role Invitation with the current browser Session

post.description: Starts a short-lived browser handoff for a Desktop client, binding the callback, opaque state, selected authentication method, device presentation, and S256 PKCE challenge. No Session is created until the browser approves the transaction and the Desktop client exchanges the one-use code.
post.summary: Create a purpose-bound Desktop browser authorization transaction

post.description: Uses the current interactive browser Session to approve the exact pending Desktop transaction identified by its handle, browser proof, and state. Approval issues a short-lived one-use code without exposing browser credentials to the Desktop client.
post.summary: Approve a Desktop transaction with the current browser Session

post.description: Cancels the exact pending Desktop transaction after validating its handle, browser proof, and state. Cancellation is terminal and prevents a later approval or token exchange for that transaction.
post.summary: Cancel one pending Desktop browser authorization transaction

post.description: Consumes the one-use Desktop authorization code only when the opaque state and PKCE verifier match the original transaction. A successful exchange creates an ordinary bounded Desktop Session; replay or mismatched proof is rejected.
post.summary: Atomically exchange one Desktop code and S256 verifier for an ordinary Desktop Session

post.description: Consumes one valid short-lived verification token and marks its bound email address verified. The token is single use, cannot verify another address, and an invalid or expired token reveals no account details.
post.summary: Consume an email-verification credential

post.description: Requests a new short-lived verification message for the authenticated User's current unverified email address. The response is deliberately non-enumerating, and any prior usable verification credential may be superseded.
post.summary: Request an email-verification message

post.description: Authenticates a local credential and creates an interactive Session for the declared client type. Browser clients receive host-only cookies while native clients may consume response tokens; MFA-enabled accounts must include a current TOTP or unused recovery code. Authentication failures do not reveal which credential was wrong.
post.summary: Create an interactive session

post.description: Revokes the exact interactive Session represented by the current access credential and clears browser authentication cookies when present. Other Sessions for the User remain active.
post.summary: Revoke the current session

post.description: Consumes one valid short-lived reset token, applies the new policy-compliant password, and revokes affected Sessions according to the authentication contract. Expired, replayed, or superseded credentials are rejected without exposing account state.
post.summary: Consume a password-reset credential

post.description: Requests a short-lived password-reset message for the supplied email address when an eligible local account exists. The accepted response is intentionally identical for known and unknown addresses to prevent account discovery.
post.summary: Request a password-reset message

get.description: Returns the public presentation of external providers currently permitted by Access Policy. Provider secrets, discovery internals, and disabled providers are omitted; clients should treat this list as dynamic.
get.summary: List external authentication providers selected by current Access Policy

get.description: Validates the provider callback, consumes the short-lived state transaction, and creates or updates only the account relationship authorized by that transaction. It then redirects to the validated client destination without exposing provider credentials.
get.summary: Complete external authentication

get.description: Creates a short-lived, state-bound external authentication transaction and redirects the browser to the selected provider. The requested return target and device presentation are validated before any redirect is issued.
get.summary: Begin external authentication

post.description: Starts external authentication bound to one Invitation claim so the eventual provider identity can accept only that immutable Invitation package. The claim is not exposed in the provider redirect or returned to another account.
post.summary: Begin invitation-bound external authentication

post.description: Atomically rotates the current Session's refresh credential and returns a fresh access/refresh pair or browser cookies. Reuse of a consumed refresh credential is treated as replay and invalidates the affected Session family.
post.summary: Rotate refresh credentials

get.description: Returns non-secret key identifiers and active encrypted-payload reference counts needed to plan or verify key rotation. Strong recent authentication is required, and no key bytes, wrapping material, ciphertext, recipients, or message content are exposed.
get.summary: Inspect safe mail payload-key identities and active reference counts

get.description: Returns bounded aggregate delivery and queue health metrics for public allowlisted template categories. Metrics contain no recipient identity, message content, payload identifiers, credentials, or raw provider errors.
get.summary: Inspect bounded mail delivery metrics

post.description: Starts one durable Job that re-encrypts active mail payloads from an explicitly retiring key to the configured primary key. Strong recent authentication and durable fencing prevent overlapping rotations or retirement without final zero-reference proof.
post.summary: Start a durable fenced mail payload-key rotation

get.description: Returns bounded progress for one authorized mail rekey Job and, after completion, the counts required to prove whether the retiring key is safe to remove. No payload content, key bytes, recipients, or worker diagnostics are returned.
get.summary: Inspect safe progress and final retirement proof for one mail rekey Job

parameters.description: The durable mail rekey Job whose safe progress is requested.
parameters.name: job_id

post.description: Durably queues the fixed test template to the current operator's verified eligible address. The server chooses the recipient and content, applies a dedicated rate limit, and returns only safe delivery metadata.
post.summary: Enqueue a controlled test message to the operator's verified address

post.description: Stores one bounded formula-safe CSV source and creates a durable validation Job for the explicit mode and authorization scope. Upload performs no account, membership, or Role mutation; the resulting immutable preview must be reviewed and committed separately.

parameters.description: Selects the onboarding workflow and therefore the CSV columns and validation rules to apply.

parameters.description: Declares the kind of resource that owns every row in this import.

post.summary: Upload a bounded onboarding CSV for asynchronous validation

get.description: Returns the bounded authorized state, preview digest, and row outcomes for one onboarding import. The projection omits original claims, passwords, mail payloads, internal Job data, and unsafe parsing diagnostics.
get.summary: Get one authorized immutable onboarding preview or final report projection

post.description: Requests cooperative cancellation while the authorized onboarding validation or commit Job remains cancelable. It cannot roll back rows that already committed and preserves the immutable source, preview, and Job history.
post.summary: Cooperatively cancel an onboarding parse or execution

post.description: Starts application of the exact immutable preview only when its revision, digest, and selected commit policy still match. Per-row transactions preserve bounded outcomes, and the operation never accepts an unvalidated or silently changed upload.
post.summary: Commit one exact validated onboarding preview

get.description: Downloads the bounded authorized preview or final row report with spreadsheet formulas neutralized as data. The report excludes credentials, one-time claims, mail payloads, and internal worker diagnostics.
get.summary: Download the authorized formula-safe onboarding report

delete.description: Archives one Programme Level only when it has no active Classes. The transition retains history and never cascades into Class archival, enrollment termination, or Role Binding removal.
delete.summary: Archive a Programme Level that has no active Classes

get.description: Returns one active Programme Level when its owning Programme hierarchy is visible to the caller. The projection does not expand Classes or confer authority over their rosters.

patch.description: Applies a partial canonical or presentation update while preserving the Level's Programme owner. Dependent Classes retain their stable parent identity and block changes that would violate current structure.
patch.summary: Update a Programme Level without changing its Programme owner

get.description: Lists active Classes directly assigned to one authorized Programme Level. The collection returns structural Class metadata and excludes rosters, candidate Attempts, and permission grants.
get.summary: List Classes for a Programme Level

post.description: Creates one concrete student roster under the Programme Level in the route and one eligible Academic Period in the body. Creation performs owner and period checks but does not enroll any student automatically.
post.summary: Create a Class for a Programme Level and Academic Period

delete.description: Archives one Programme only after proving it has no active Programme Levels. The operation retains history and never cascades into Level, Class, enrollment, or authorization changes.
delete.summary: Archive a Programme that has no active Programme Levels

get.description: Returns one active Programme when its owning Academic Unit is visible to the current principal. The bounded projection does not expand Levels or Classes.
get.summary: Get a Programme

patch.description: Applies a partial canonical or presentation update while preserving the Programme's Academic Unit owner. Dependent Levels retain stable ownership and are not mutated by this command.
patch.summary: Update a Programme without changing its Academic Unit owner

get.description: Lists active Levels directly owned by one authorized Programme with bounded stable search. The collection excludes Classes and does not imply roster or permission access.

parameters.name: limit

get.summary: List or search Programme Levels owned by a Programme

post.description: Creates one Level under the exact Programme in the route after rechecking management authority. It does not create Classes, Academic Periods, enrollments, or permission grants.

get.description: Lists current and historical Role Bindings authorized for the caller, optionally narrowed to one User or exact scope. A Binding is an effective-dated permission grant; membership or affiliation alone is not returned as authority.

post.summary: Create a Role Binding

delete.description: Ends the exact Role Binding while retaining its grant history and durable audit provenance. The server prevents removal of the final effective system administrator and does not alter the underlying User, Role, membership, or affiliation.

get.description: Lists built-in and custom Roles visible to the authorized caller. Role definitions name permissions only; effective access also requires a current scoped Role Binding and terminal authorization against current durable state.
get.summary: List Roles

post.description: Creates a reusable custom Role from a canonical name and an allowlisted set of known permissions. Creation grants the Role to nobody; a separate scoped Role Binding is required before it affects authorization.
post.summary: Create a custom Role

delete.description: Deletes an unprotected custom Role only when no retained Binding dependency prevents removal. Built-in Roles and Roles whose deletion would invalidate active authorization history remain protected.

get.description: Returns one built-in or custom Role visible to the caller, including its current permission set and built-in protection flag. The response does not imply that any User currently holds the Role.
get.summary: Get a Role

patch.description: Changes the presentation or complete permission set of one custom Role after rechecking current authority. Built-in Roles are protected, and a permission change can fail when active historical guarantees make the proposed replacement unsafe.

post.description: Creates a durable Job that validates the exact source and destination Classes and Academic Periods without changing enrollment. Its immutable preview and digest expose bounded row outcomes for review before commit.
post.summary: Create an asynchronous dry-run for one exact student progression

get.description: Returns the authorized immutable preview or terminal result for one progression Job. The projection is bounded and contains no credentials, student answers, or unsafe worker diagnostics.
get.summary: Get one authorized student progression preview or result

post.description: Requests cancellation of one authorized progression while its dry-run or commit work is still cancelable. Cancellation is cooperative, preserves the preview and Job history, and cannot roll back a completed enrollment transaction.
post.summary: Cooperatively cancel a student progression

post.description: Applies the exact authorized dry-run preview only when its revision and digest still match current source, destination, and student state. The named aggregate transition ends and creates enrollments atomically and preserves history for every affected student.
post.summary: Commit one exact student progression preview

get.description: Downloads the bounded report for one authorized progression preview or result with spreadsheet formulas neutralized as data. The response contains the reviewed row projection and no internal Job payload, credentials, or database selectors.
get.summary: Download the authorized formula-safe student progression report

post.summary: Freeze the complete Review and bounded evidence inventory

post.description: Releases the narrow approved candidate result from one finalized Review revision. The transition does not expose manager notes, rationales, Flags, evidence, Discrepancies, or other private review state.
post.summary: Explicitly release the approved candidate result projection

get.description: Returns the release version and immutable build provenance for the currently serving node. The response contains no runtime configuration, credentials, dependency addresses, or installation identity.

get.summary: Get the authenticated User profile

get.description: Returns whether MFA is active, whether a setup is pending, and the count of unused recovery codes for the current User. TOTP secrets and recovery-code values are never returned by this status view.
get.summary: Get current-user MFA status

post.description: Verifies a current TOTP code against the pending setup, activates MFA, and returns a new recovery-code set exactly once. An expired or superseded setup cannot be activated.
post.summary: Activate pending MFA setup

post.description: Verifies a current TOTP code or one unused recovery code and upgrades the exact current interactive Session to MFA assurance. A recovery code is consumed atomically and cannot be replayed.
post.summary: Upgrade the current session with MFA

post.description: Disables MFA for the current User after strong recent authentication and invalidates pending setup material and recovery codes. The transition is audited and may be blocked by current policy.
post.summary: Disable current-user MFA

It requires a strong, recently authenticated interactive Session; Personal Access Tokens cannot satisfy that assurance. Store the returned codes securely because Proctor does not expose them again.
post.summary: Regenerate MFA recovery codes

post.description: Creates or replaces a short-lived pending TOTP setup and returns its secret and provisioning URI exactly for enrollment. MFA is not active until a valid code is submitted to the activation operation.
post.summary: Begin MFA setup

get.summary: List the current user's sessions

post.description: Revokes every active Session belonging to the current User, including the Session making the request. Clients must discard cached credentials and require a new authentication flow afterward.

get.summary: List current-user Personal Access Tokens

post.description: Creates a bounded Personal Access Token after recent interactive authentication and returns its credential exactly once. Requested scopes and any Academic Unit boundary are validated against current authority and policy.
post.summary: Create a Personal Access Token

delete.description: Permanently revokes the exact Personal Access Token belonging to the current User. Revocation is durable and audited; the credential cannot be restored or exchanged for a replacement.

post.description: Temporarily disables the exact current-User Personal Access Token so its credential can no longer authenticate. The token record and audit history remain available for later review or re-enablement.
post.summary: Disable a Personal Access Token

post.description: Re-enables a disabled, unexpired Personal Access Token after recent interactive authentication and a fresh scope-authority check. Revoked tokens cannot be enabled.

get.description: Lists the authorized current and historical relationship kinds attached to one User. Affiliations are non-exclusive descriptive relationships and never substitute for Role Bindings in permission checks.

post.description: Adds one effective-dated student, teacher, staff, or external relationship to an existing User. Other Affiliation kinds may coexist, and the transition grants no permissions or credentials by itself.

post.description: Disables the target User and atomically revokes active Sessions after checking current authority and last-system-administrator safety. Historical affiliations, memberships, Role Bindings, attempts, submissions, and audit records are retained.

post.description: Marks the target User's current email as verified through a distinct strongly authenticated administrative transition. It does not change the address, revive a disabled account, restore Sessions, or bypass current authorization.

post.description: Enables a previously disabled User after terminal authorization. The transition preserves history but does not restore revoked Sessions, verify email, add authentication methods, reactivate ended relationships, or recreate Role Bindings.
post.summary: Enable a User account without restoring revoked sessions
